## About Me

I am a quantitative analyst with training in applied mathematics and political science from UCLA. My work focuses on forecasting under uncertainty, building scalable operational systems, and translating complex data into strategic insights for diverse stakeholders. I have recently been experimenting extensively with AI agents like Gemini 3.5 Flash and Claude Opus 4.6 in Google Antigravity to build new games and tools to share with the world.

With experience spanning climate consulting at Clark Street Associates, NGO alliance development in Argentina, and large-scale program operations at UCLA, I combine rigorous mathematical modeling with policy analysis. I am passionate about leveraging  data systems to solve today's challenges, and believe that AI is the power tool to do so quickly and efficiently.

In my spare time, besides developing new tools to share, I also care for my dog Libby and have recently done several car repairs (engine drive belt replacement, gasket cover replacement, + more) with Dad in the driveway. For sport, I joined Quadball in my third year at UCLA, and I am continuing to play now with the Silicon Valley Vipers!

### Core Skills & Technologies
Antigravity/Codex, Python, R, SQL, Excel/Sheets, C++, JavaScript, Spanish

## Projects

### Aetherium: Steam & Shadow
- Subtitle: Steampunk RTS Battle Game
- Status: Completed / Active
- Technologies: HTML5 Canvas, Vanilla CSS3, Vanilla Javascript, Web Audio API
- Live URL: https://frankhobson.github.io/Aetherium/
- Source Code: https://github.com/frankhobson/Aetherium

Lead the steam-powered Alchemical Empire against the invading Gothic Necromancy Crypt Horde in this browser-based real-time strategy combat game. Battle for control of central Aether Geysers, research advanced technologies, and deploy the colossal Gilded Behemoth to secure your keep and claim victory!

### Global Elections Model
- Subtitle: A correlation study between global events and election results
- Status: Completed / Active
- Technologies: Python, Streamlit, Machine Learning, GDELT API, V-Dem Database, Predictive Modeling
- Live URL: https://frankhobson.github.io/elections/
- Source Code: https://github.com/frankhobson/elections

This elections research project aims to predict election results based off of prevailing global patterns rather than race-specific polling. The project uses the Global Database of Events, Language, and Tone, but does not include any specifics on candidate quality or even the political leaning of different parties. Instead, the model hopes to predict when people want a change in their national government. Currently, the model sits around 70% accuracy.
